t:
(a) Prevention of Harmful Interference.—Not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating, acting through the Commandant of the Coast Guard, may transfer $1,000,000 to the National Telecommunications and Information Administration of the Department of Commerce for the purposes of awarding, not later than 120 days after such date of enactment, a competitive grant to design and develop a prototype device that integrates a Class B Automatic Identification System transponder (International Electrotechnical Commission standard 62287) with a wireless maritime data device approved by the Federal Communications Commission with channel throughput greater than 19.2 kilobits per second to enable such wireless maritime data device to provide wireless maritime data services, concurrent with the operation of the transponder, on frequency channels adjacent to the frequency channels on which the transponder operates, while minimizing or eliminating the harmful interference between the transponder and such wireless maritime data device. The design of the device developed under this subsection shall be available for public use. 
    (b) Implementation of AIS.—It is the sense of the Senate, not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act, that the Federal Communications Commission should resolve the disposition of its rulemaking on the Automatic Information System and licensee use of frequency bands 157.1875–157.4375 MHz and 161.7875–162.0375 MHz (RM–10821, WT Docket Number 04–344). 
The implementation of this section shall not delay the implementation of an Automatic Identification System as required by section 70114 of title 46, United States Code, and international convention.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the reference to an FCC "rulemaking" signals public participation. But this is only a non-binding sense of the Senate urging the FCC to conclude an already pending docket; it does not grant new rulemaking authority or require a new comment period, hearing, or outside consultation. The rest of the section concerns an intra-federal transfer of funds and a competitive grant, and grant applications are not participation. Making the device design "available for public use" does not bring outsiders into a federal decision.
fable.s: the Federal Communications Commission should resolve the disposition of its rulemaking on the Automatic Information System

opus.w: Subsection (b) recommends that the FCC finish a pending rulemaking docket. Under the definition, rulemaking counts as participation because it involves notice and comment from outside parties, and the question covers recommendations as well as requirements. The tempting 'No' reading looks only at subsection (a), where the fund transfer and competitive grant really are excluded as intra-government action and a grant application. That reading misses the rulemaking in (b).
opus.s: It is the sense of the Senate, not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act, that the Federal Communications Commission should resolve the disposition of its rulemaking on the Automatic Information System and licensee use of frequency bands 157.1875–157.4375 MHz and 161.7875–162.0375 MHz (RM–10821, WT Docket Number 04–344).
opus.b:
**Label: Yes.** The section recommends that the FCC finish a rulemaking, and the definition counts rulemaking as participation.

1. **The tempting reading, and why it fails.** It is tempting to stop at subsection (a). That part only covers a fund transfer between federal agencies and a competitive grant. Both are excluded: one stays inside the government, and grant applications are not participation. On that reading the answer would be "No." But subsection (b) tells the FCC to resolve a specific pending rulemaking with a docket number (WT Docket No. 04-344). A rulemaking docket gives outside parties a notice-and-comment period. The question asks whether the section recommends or requires participation, so the "should" language in a sense-of-the-Senate provision is enough.
2. **Remaining doubt.** The provision does not create a new comment process. It only urges the FCC to wrap up one that already exists, and it is non-binding.

qwen_chat.w: The section expresses the 'sense of the Senate' regarding FCC rulemaking, but the Senate is inside the federal government, so this does not constitute participation by an outside party. The grant provision in subsection (a) involves a competitive award process, which is excluded from the definition of participation as it relates to applications for grants. There is no requirement for public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes/public before the federal decision.
qwen_chat.s: It is the sense of the Senate, not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act, that the Federal Communications Commission should resolve the disposition of its rulemaking on the Automatic Information System
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "It is the sense of the Senate... that the Federal Communications Commission should resolve..." implies a form of consultation or coordination with an outside entity (the Senate) regarding a federal decision. However, the Senate is part of the federal government (legislative branch), and "sense of the Senate" resolutions are non-binding expressions of opinion, not mandatory consultation processes involving non-federal parties. Furthermore, the grant process described in (a) is a competitive award mechanism, which falls under the "applications for benefits or grants" exclusion in the definition. The public availability of the design is a result, not a participatory process.
